svg.title: Grants (v1.3): issuing by the owner, delegating with attenuation only, checking at every point of action, revoking

g.text: Grants (v1.3): issuing by the owner, delegating with attenuation only, checking at every point of action, revoking
separate grants, actions[] entries from the register:
session.input for session X; session.approve bound to target.execution_id;
session.control for the concrete control target; expires_at, delegable: no
The subject uses an operator key enrolled for the binding (ADM §§3-4).
transcript is the binding audience projection (ADM §7),
separate from session action authority; no generic operator action.
verify owner signature; append; new revocation snapshot id
snapshot refresh (broker, host, dispatcher, core subscribe)
sign grant {issuer: orch_a, subject: w_17, action: post to thread t,
target: room r, expiry ≤ own} (peer UID → key of orch_a)
check: orch_a holds a delegable grant covering
(action, target) ⊇ the new grant? expiry not longer?
check at the point of action
spawn role R in P by orch_a? requested child grants ⊆ delegable?
enqueue user_turn to X by sender S? (session.input, fresh, not revoked)
may S write to a_7? (post/mailbox grant)
may run R move element E from s1 to s2? (role grant under the flow version)
One verification library everywhere: parse, verify the signature
chain to the root, check expiry and conditions, consult the
revocation snapshot. The requester never judges its own request.
signed revocation of the grant (or of an identity)
refresh; in-flight items re-admitted at dispatch against the new snapshot
